dispositions.method: Round two of 1808. On 11 November 2026 the owner set the rule 'every story alike': a reviewed story is described by what kind of text it is and whose account, in the papers' own words, never as what happened; sensitive subjects get no special treatment. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. As before, an excerpt ends before the names of private people where it can, and stories that turn on private people stay out. The three items round one left out for framing were read again with phrase searches over all 4,466 pages filed under 1808 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), every hit was read, the papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords (no missed printing), and every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/batch_13.json and batch_14.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round2.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: As in round one: a story needs one printed item found in 7 or more newspapers, counted item by item. All three reach 7 and are admitted as new top-level stories; the parent story of round one on the charges against General Wilkinson names its children in its definition and stays as released.
